key_facts: Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, will price its shares at $83 each for a Nasdaq listing on Thursday, implying a valuation of at least $1.4 trillion (£1.1 trillion); the earlier indicative range was $70–$78 per share, valuing the company at up to $1.3tn.

According to one early investor speaking on condition of anonymity, shares were more than 10 times oversubscribed; the company expects to raise over $68bn from its IPO plus another $26bn from private placements, for a total of about $94bn.

It would be the first US company focused exclusively on AI to go public; SpaceX's June debut at $2.2tn is the reference point, though SpaceX shares fell significantly in the following weeks. OpenAI is expected to go public next year.

Analysts flagged concerns about whether Anthropic's revenue and profits can keep pace with hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations due over the next couple of years; the Federal Reserve expressed concern about AI-related debt financed through 'complex and opaque' structures and concentration among a small number of firms.
importance_reason: Крупнейший IPO AI-компании с оценкой $1.4tn и системными опасениями регулятора по долговой нагрузке сектора.
market_link: Оценка и приём IPO могут задать ориентир для AI-сегмента Nasdaq; опасения ФРС по AI-долгу и концентрации рисков способны влиять на кредитные рынки и широкие индексы акций.

key_facts: The Scottish government plans to issue its first bonds (nicknamed "kilts"), aiming to raise about £1.5bn by the end of the parliamentary term, to fund long-term capital projects such as hospitals and road maintenance; it expects issuance within this financial year, subject to market conditions.

The government's capital borrowing limit is up to £450m a year at 2023-24 levels, with a total cap of £3bn uprated for inflation; the government has an identical credit rating to the UK's. Estimates cited in the article put kilt interest rates 0.3 percentage points above gilts, plus £2m per bond in administrative costs; the government has not published its own costings.

Critics, including Conservative MSP Liam Kerr, questioned whether the bonds would be more expensive than borrowing via the National Loans Fund and raised transparency concerns; experts said independence could materially change the risk profile of the bonds.
importance_reason: Regional sub-sovereign debt issuance with limited scale (£1.5bn against a ~£70bn budget) and no direct market-moving effect.
